item.title: "Case Is Being Actively Reviewed": what this USCIS status means and what to do
item.description: Your USCIS status says Case Is Being Actively Reviewed. What it means, why it can repeat, how long it may take, and what to do while you wait.

item.title: "Case Was Received": what it means when USCIS receives your case and what comes next
item.description: Your USCIS status says Case Was Received. What it means, which receipt notice arrives, how to use your receipt date for processing times, and what to do next.

item.title: "Case Was Approved": what a USCIS approval means and what happens next
item.description: Your USCIS status says Case Was Approved. What it means for your form (I-130, I-485, I-765, N-400), which notice arrives, and the next step.

item.title: "Case Was Transferred": what it means when USCIS moves your case to another office
item.description: Your USCIS status says your case was transferred. What it means, why it happens, whether your receipt number or timeline changes, and what to do next.

item.title: How to ask USCIS to expedite your case: a simple guide
item.description: What a USCIS expedite request is, which reasons USCIS accepts, how to ask, what evidence to send, and what to do if your case is just slow.

item.title: Form I-539: how to extend your stay or change your nonimmigrant status in the U.S.
item.description: Simple guide to USCIS Form I-539: who uses it, when to file before your I-94 expires, who cannot use it, and what happens next.

item.title: Citizenship (N-400): new USCIS memo on good moral character, public benefits, child support and sponsorship
item.description: On November 4, 2026, USCIS issued memo PM-602-0201 on good moral character for citizenship: public benefits, dependent support and sponsor duties.

item.title: Form I-693 medical exam for a green card: who does it, when, and what to bring
item.description: Simple guide to the I-693 immigration medical exam: the authorized civil surgeon, filing it with Form I-485, vaccines, cost, and common mistakes.

item.title: Form I-864 Affidavit of Support for a green card: a simple guide
item.description: What Form I-864 is, who can sponsor, the 125% income rule, joint sponsors, Form I-864A, and when the sponsor's obligation ends.

item.title: 60-day grace period for H-1B, L-1, O-1 and TN: DHS proposes to remove it (comments due November 10)
item.description: DHS proposes removing the up-to-60-day grace period after a job ends for H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN and E workers. Not in effect yet. Comments due November 10, 2026.

item.title: Form I-131 (travel permit / advance parole): how to leave the U.S. without losing your case
item.description: A simple I-131 guide: advance parole, reentry permit and refugee travel document. Who needs it, when to file and what to avoid.

item.title: Form I-751: how to remove conditions on your 2-year green card (marriage)
item.description: A simple I-751 guide: when to file (90 days before expiry), filing without your spouse, the 48-month extension, and what happens if you don't file.

item.title: DV-2027 green card lottery still closed after an appeals court pause
item.description: DV-2027 green card lottery registration did not open on November 1. An appeals court paused the order. What happened and how to avoid scams.

item.title: USCIS green card interview (I-485): what to bring, what happens and what comes next
item.description: A simple guide to the adjustment of status (I-485) interview: original documents to bring, what they ask and what happens after.

item.title: Investor green card (EB-5): new USCIS fees start November 30, 2026
item.description: USCIS raises EB-5 fees (I-526, I-526E, I-829, I-956) starting Nov. 30, 2026. What changes, who it affects, and what to do before you file.

item.title: "Card Was Mailed To Me": USCIS sent your green card or work permit. How to track it and what to do if it doesn't arrive
item.description: What the "Card Was Mailed To Me" status means, how to track your green card or work permit with USPS, and what to do if it doesn't arrive.

item.title: USCIS reports 2.2 million enforcement actions: what it means for your case
item.description: On Oct. 29, 2026, USCIS reported about 2.2 million actions to revoke or end status. What it includes, what it is not, and what to do.

item.title: Form I-90: how to renew or replace your green card (and the 36-month extension)
item.description: A simple I-90 guide: when to renew your green card, who should not use it, how to file, and how the receipt extends your card 36 months.

item.title: Form I-485 (adjustment of status): how to apply for a green card inside the U.S.
item.description: A simple guide to Form I-485: who files, when a visa is available, biometrics, the interview and what happens next. No made-up dates.

item.title: Form N-400 (citizenship): requirements, when to apply and the steps
item.description: A simple guide to Form N-400 to apply for U.S. citizenship: 5-year rules, filing 90 days early, the test, the interview and the oath.

item.title: Form I-765 (work permit): who files it, how to renew and what to expect
item.description: A simple guide to Form I-765 to apply for or renew a work permit (EAD): what it is, when to renew and how to track your USCIS case.

item.title: Employment green card (PERM): what the Instacart and Cloudera settlements mean
item.description: The government settled with Instacart and Cloudera over PERM recruiting. Here is what PERM is and what to do if your employer sponsors you.

item.title: Form I-130 (family petition): who can sponsor a relative and what happens next
item.description: A simple guide to Form I-130 to sponsor a relative for a green card: who can file, what approval means and how long the wait can be.

item.title: USCIS biometrics (fingerprint) appointment: what to bring, what happens and how to reschedule
item.description: A simple guide to the USCIS fingerprint appointment: what to bring, what happens at the ASC and how to reschedule before the date.

item.title: OPT for F-1 students: DHS proposes a $70,000 fee (not in effect yet; comments due November 9)
item.description: DHS proposes schools pay $70,000 for each F-1 student's first OPT and $30,000 for later ones. It is only a proposal. What to do.

item.title: USCIS Form I-797C (Notice of Action): what it means and what to do when you get one
item.description: Form I-797C is USCIS's notice for receipts, rejections, transfers and appointments. It is not an approval. Learn to read it and what to do.

item.title: Ukraine and Sudan TPS after October 19, 2026: work permits remain valid for now
item.description: USCIS says Ukraine and Sudan TPS holders keep their protection and work authorization until a new announcement. What changed and what to do.

item.title: November 2026 Visa Bulletin: EB-2 and EB-3 final action dates advance for the green card
item.description: EB-2 Rest of World and Mexico: April 1, 2025 (final action). EB-3: June 15, 2024. Employment Dates for Filing hold steady.

item.title: USCIS raises work permit, TPS, asylum and parole fees starting October 16, 2026
item.description: Starting October 16, 2026, some H.R. 1 fees go up: initial EAD to $570, TPS to $520 and parole to $1,050. Table of changes and what to do.

item.title: USCIS changes filing deadlines that fall on a weekend or holiday starting October 23, 2026
item.description: From October 23, only deadlines counted in days move to the next business day. Age or status-expiration cutoffs do not. What changes and what to do.
